note: From OpenStreetMap's main API (13 October 2026), 1.25 times real across the line like the tracks: two side platforms of about 95 m on the Buxton line, 2.1 m outside its two tracks (trains stop 10 m north of the station's point, in the middle of them, so a four-car unit stands on them as they are; a six-car one stands off the end, as at a real short platform, which `longest` says), in a wooded cutting, with the Middlewood Way (the old Macclesfield, Bollington and Marple line, now a path) crossing over the station on its bridge at an angle. Positive v is north here. There's no road to it: from the halt's platform (towards Manchester) steps climb the cutting to the Way, and a path leaves the platform's east end along the line; the other platform has a ramp down from the Way. Views from above (docs/reference/aerial/middlewood.jpg, the LIDAR surface model): the line curving through the woods, the Way's bridge, fields all round. Photos (docs/reference/photos/middlewood: geograph 7061925 and 7061922 Chris Morgan 2022, 7058408 Peter McDermott 2022, 6703337 Benjamin Shaw 2019, 5656302, 5656307 and 5656324 Stephen Craven 2016): tarmac platforms with low fences (timber on one, black railings on the other), one small white shelter, tall lamp columns; drawn on the halt's platform, though which side it stands is not settled by the photos. No canopy, kiosk, barriers, lifts or extension at the real station: the game's. The bridge's brick from memory. The Way's bridge stands high over flat ground until the real cutting is drawn here (the real surroundings tool hasn't run beyond Hazel Grove yet: pick-up item 7); the cycle stands from OpenStreetMap (10).

parts.note: Middlewood has no road: the replacement buses stand where the lane from Middlewood Road ends, about 80 m from the platforms by the path, the nearest a bus can come (OpenStreetMap); the stop is the game's
